regimens.indication: Acute Ischemic Stroke (AIS, initiated as soon as possible within 3 hours after symptom onset)

refs.quote: Activase is indicated for the treatment of acute ischemic stroke. Exclude intracranial hemorrhage as the primary cause of stroke signs and symptoms prior to initiation of treatment [see Contraindications (4.1) ] . Initiate treatment as soon as possible but within 3 hours after symptom onset.
The recommended dose is 0.9 mg/kg (not to exceed 90 mg total dose), with 10% of the total dose administered as an initial intravenous bolus over 1 minute and the remainder infused over 60 minutes.

regimens.dose_text: 0.9 mg/kg (maximum total dose 90 mg): 10% of the calculated total dose administered as an IV bolus over 1 minute, followed by the remaining 90% infused continuously over 60 minutes. Monitor blood pressure frequently during and after infusion.

refs.quote: Alteplase is a serine protease responsible for fibrin-enhanced conversion of plasminogen to plasmin. It produces limited conversion of plasminogen in the absence of fibrin.

mg_safety.note: Thrombolytic agents do not impair neuromuscular junction transmission; safe in myasthenia gravis

ng_tube.note: Intravenous solution only; not for enteral administration

mechanism_of_action.value: Alteplase is a serine protease responsible for fibrin-enhanced conversion of plasminogen to plasmin. It produces limited conversion of plasminogen in the absence of fibrin. When introduced into the systemic circulation at pharmacologic concentration, alteplase binds to fibrin in a thrombus and converts the entrapped plasminogen to plasmin. This initiates local fibrinolysis.

Activase is for intravenous administration only. Do not add any other medication to infusion solutions containing Activase. Extravasation of Activase infusion can cause ecchymosis or inflammation. If extravasation occurs, terminate the infusion at that intravenous site and apply local therapy. Use within 8 hours following reconstitution (when stored at 2–30°C).
